extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting journal articles (particularly to Sage journals); academic researchers preparing minor revisions after peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors on what constitutes a 'minor revision' decision and how to prepare a resubmission: writing a point-by-point response, making targeted manuscript edits, checking journal requirements, communicating with editors, and proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguities in the text
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguities in the text, requiring re-writing to address specific areas where the manuscript requires clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite unclear passages to directly address reviewers' points; target specific sections and make the intended meaning explicit so reviewers and editors can see the issue resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjusting citations that could be limited, excessive, out of date, or require reformatting in line with the journal’s reference style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citations are current, appropriately scoped, and formatted to the journal's style. The journal submission pages (e.g., 'preparing your manuscript for submission') give reference style details; use tools like the Sage EndNote output file to format references correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting simple factual or numerical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Correcting simple factual or numerical errors, which are easily resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix erroneous numbers or factual mistakes and indicate the corrections in your response so reviewers can verify the change quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting issues with tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting issues with tables and figures i.e., incorrect labelling, missing arrows, enhancing figure quality, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct labels, add missing annotations (e.g., arrows), and improve image quality or layout to meet journal presentation standards; reference the exact figure/table and location in your response document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor language edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor language edits such as repetitive statements, typos, subject-specific formatting conventions, spelling errors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove repetition, correct typos/spelling, and apply subject-specific formatting conventions. Thorough proofreading (see separate tip) is recommended to ensure polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a clear response document and address each comment systematically
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a clear response document and address each comment systematically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your response document should read like a conversation with the reviewer: explain why you made changes, not just state 'done'. Point to the exact location of revisions (e.g., 'We’ve added a sentence in Section 2 to clarify the methodology... Correction: Page 3, lines 5-10'). A well-organised document shows careful consideration and helps the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek clarification from the editor when reviewer comments are ambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: If something is unclear, seek clarification from the journal editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't guess at reviewers' intentions — politely and specifically ask the editor for clarification (example phrasing provided). This avoids unnecessary revisions and further rounds of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check journal-specific guidelines and required statements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify journal-specific formatting per article type and reference style. Ensure required elements are present and correct: acknowledgements, declaration of conflicting interest, funding statement, ethical approval and informed consent (if applicable). Use the journal website's 'preparing your manuscript for submission' instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for a timely resubmission (and communicate if you can’t)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a timely resubmission (but communicate if you can’t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the journal's deadlines to keep the process moving. Set a personal deadline; if unable to meet it, contact the editor in advance to explain and request more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly proofread your manuscript
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a final review for grammar, spelling, and formatting accuracy so the manuscript is polished before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear evidence that reviewer suggestions have been addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions give you an opportunity to improve your paper in light of the comments you receive, so show the editor and reviewers plenty of evidence that you have done so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the response document to document changes (locations, excerpts), explain rationale for edits, and demonstrate how reviewer concerns have been resolved; this evidence helps the editor decide on acceptance without additional rounds of review.
